data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Separating authoring and checking engines may actually decrease verification reliability due to 'Competence Asymmetry', where a separate checker lacks the specific internal context required to spot a nuanced error.","counterconditions":[{"case":"Model B is significantly more capable (higher parameter count/better training) than Model A.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Model A is consistently blinded by its own biases during self-correction.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"A separate engine (Model B) may be more likely to 'rubber-stamp' a complex but wrong claim from Model A because it lacks the specific 'cognitive path' Model A took to reach the error. Conversely, Model A, checking itself, can trace its own logic and find the exact point of failure. Verification is thus distinguished from restatement by the 'Depth of Trace'\u2014whether the checker identifies the specific step of failure rather than just the wrong final answer.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
